object_context: Child of BSD-A1a-KATO-NONVANISHING-BRIDGE. For an elliptic curve E/Q with exact complex analytic rank two, determine whether current source-bound theorems can force ord_T Theta_{f/K}=2 for an admissible anticyclotomic theta element without assuming positive Mordell-Weil rank, Selmer dimension two, BSD, or an Iwasawa/p-adic BSD statement of equivalent arithmetic strength.
structural_coordinates: the root input ord_{s=1} L(E,s)=2 is a vanishing-order statement in the complex spectral variable s
Theta_{f/K}(T) is a one-variable anticyclotomic p-adic theta element with T defined by a topological generator of Gamma_infinity; ord_T is a character-deformation order at T=0
Castella-Hsieh Theorem 2.3 interpolates central values L(f/K tensor chi epsilon_zeta,1) at finite-order anticyclotomic characters zeta, so T varies character and not the complex variable s
under the Castella-Hsieh hypotheses L(E/K,1)=0 implies only ord_T Theta_{f/K}>0 from interpolation; the source does not infer ord_T=2 from complex analytic rank two

Castella-Hsieh Theorem B requires ord_T Theta_{f/K}=2 and rank_Z E(Q)>0 to conclude generalized-Kato nonvanishing, so it cannot itself provide an analytic-rank-two-to-arithmetic-rank bridge without circularity
the triple-product p-adic L-function factorization isolates Theta_{f/K} times explicitly nonzero auxiliary factors once auxiliary nonvanishing hypotheses hold

the Coleman/explicit-reciprocity law transports Theta_{f/K} into the localization of the big diagonal-cycle/generalized-Kato system, but nonzero transport still depends on the exact theta leading term and local map
the root-bridge stability tool is relevant only as a diagnostic: a root-critical coordinate must be shown to survive a change of representation rather than assumed to do so
the target is a theorem comparing two different deformation directions, not a numerical verification of theta order on selected rank-two curves
any admissible K, p, chi selection theorem must be separated from the theta-order comparison itself
equivalent_formulations: find a theorem whose hypotheses follow from exact complex analytic rank two plus explicit admissibility conditions and whose conclusion is ord_T Theta_{f/K}=2
identify an exact comparison formula linking the first nonzero complex s-derivative of L(E,s) at order two to the first nonzero anticyclotomic T-coefficient of Theta_{f/K}
prove that the existing interpolation formula plus known nonvanishing/functional-equation input determines only positive T-order and isolate the extra theorem needed for exact T-order two
classify any Iwasawa-main-conjecture or p-adic-BSD input that determines ord_T Theta by whether it imports Selmer/Mordell-Weil information equivalent to the desired BSD bridge
solved_analogues: rank one Gross-Zagier: a complex central derivative is related to the Neron-Tate height of a canonical Heegner point under exact hypotheses
finite-order interpolation of anticyclotomic theta elements: Castella-Hsieh Theorem 2.3 identifies theta values at anticyclotomic characters with central Rankin-Selberg values
near_solved_analogues: Castella-Hsieh Theorem 5.3 gives the leading theta term against anticyclotomic derived p-adic heights once r=ord_T Theta is known
Castella-Hsieh Theorem B converts ord_T Theta=2 into generalized-Kato nonvanishing only after assuming positive Mordell-Weil rank
Castella 2023/2026 relates generalized-Kato nonvanishing to two-dimensional p-adic Selmer structure and shows the converse requires nonzero localization

method_transfers.method: evaluate a p-adic theta element at finite-order anticyclotomic characters and identify the squared value with a normalized complex central Rankin-Selberg value
shared_structure: both sides encode central L-value information for the same modular/anticyclotomic family
the trivial character detects central vanishing
required_assumptions: p and the relevant levels/discriminants satisfy the prime-to conditions
N^- is a squarefree product of an odd number of primes
disanalogies: T parametrizes anticyclotomic characters whereas s is the complex L-function variable
value interpolation at finite-order characters does not by itself identify derivatives in the T direction
complex analytic rank two for L(E,s) is not the same datum as character-direction order for Theta_{f/K}
method_transfers.repair_question: What additional source theorem identifies the exact T-adic leading order from the complex s-adic order, rather than only showing Theta(0)=0?
source_anchors: Castella-Hsieh, Forum Math. Sigma 10 (2022), Theorem 2.3, DOI 10.1017/fms.2021.85

method_transfers.method: use ord_T Theta_{f/K}=2 together with derived p-adic heights and localization to force a nonzero generalized Kato class
shared_structure: theta leading order is the p-adic analytic discriminator immediately upstream of generalized-Kato nonvanishing
derived heights encode the first nonzero anticyclotomic term
disanalogies: positive Mordell-Weil rank is downstream arithmetic information not supplied by the bare analytic-rank-two premise
the criterion consumes the theta-order statement rather than proving it
the p-adic derived-height output is not the complex BSD leading term
method_transfers.repair_question: Can theta order two be proved before and independently of positive Mordell-Weil rank/localization, or must this route remain conditional?
source_anchors: Castella-Hsieh, Forum Math. Sigma 10 (2022), Theorem B and Theorem 5.3, DOI 10.1017/fms.2021.85

method_transfers.method: separate a valid surrogate coordinate from the root coordinate and demand an explicit preservation theorem before transfer
shared_structure: a locally valid representation carries only part of the root-critical information
the target conclusion depends on a nontrivial bridge between differently normalized or parameterized objects
required_assumptions: the source and target coordinates are explicitly defined
the calibration is treated as an inference-form audit rather than a theorem about the target theory
disanalogies: the source failure concerned continuum normalization in Yang-Mills whereas the BSD target concerns different analytic deformation variables
no literal limiting sequence or spectral-gap argument transfers
the cross-problem tool supplies only an audit procedure
method_transfers.repair_question: Does the cited BSD theorem actually preserve exact vanishing order across the s-to-T representation change, and if not what is the weakest missing comparison statement?

explicit_disanalogies: ord_{s=1} and ord_T are derivatives/orders in different variables and cannot be identified by notation
finite-character interpolation constrains function values on a p-adic character family; it does not automatically identify the T-adic Taylor order at the trivial character
Theorem B assumes positive rational rank and therefore cannot be used as an unconditional analytic-to-arithmetic bridge
a numerical computation of ord_T Theta=2 for curves already known to have algebraic rank two is calibration, not a proof from analytic rank two
an Iwasawa main conjecture can determine theta/Selmer characteristic data only at the logical strength actually proved and may import arithmetic information independent of complex analytic rank
auxiliary nonvanishing selection and the theta-order comparison are separate obligations
source_anchors: Clay Mathematics Institute, official Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer problem description by Andrew Wiles
Castella-Hsieh, Forum Math. Sigma 10 (2022), Theorems 2.3, B, 5.3 and Appendix, DOI 10.1017/fms.2021.85

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: Knowing how strongly a signal vanishes when scanned along one coordinate does not determine its vanishing order along a transverse coordinate unless a calibrated relation between the scan directions is available.
common_abstraction: one object is observed through two deformation coordinates
a transfer theorem is required to preserve exact order across coordinates
source_to_target_mapping: first scan direction -> complex variable s near 1
second scan direction -> anticyclotomic character coordinate T near 0
calibration relation -> an exact comparison/reciprocity theorem controlling leading terms
shared_constraints: zero value at the common base point is weaker than equality of vanishing order
higher-order information can be lost under projection to values
a directional comparison must be proved rather than inferred from shared central values
disanalogies: the arithmetic objects are not a single smooth real multivariable function
p-adic and complex analytic geometries differ
auxiliary characters and local Euler factors enter the arithmetic interpolation
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Treat complex s-order and anticyclotomic T-order as independent coordinates until a source theorem binds their leading terms.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: For every proposed s-to-T bridge, state the exact theorem, its domain and hypotheses, the coefficient/leading-term identity it proves, and a counterexample or kernel mode showing what would fail without that theorem.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Proposal-only structural analogy; no BSD theorem authority.

analogy_scan_notes: The exact interpolation formula and the source's own conclusion r>0 were contrasted with Theorem B's stronger input r=2. The retained analogy is used only to prevent coordinate conflation. A generic bivariate calibration such as F(s,T)=(s-1)^2+T^4 shows that order two along s does not determine order two along T without extra structure; this is an inference-form calibration, not a model of the arithmetic L-functions.
